projects.name: UC Santa Cruz
projects.role: Episodic memory research with Professor Leilani H. Gilpin
projects.intro: Training and evaluating models that answer questions about images.
projects.alt: FiLM model-selection accuracy across 80 training epochs on CLEVR
projects.caption: Saved FiLM training history. The right panel shows epochs 20–80.

sections.title: My work
paragraphs: As part of the AIEA Lab's episodic memory research, I worked through visual question-answering tasks on CLEVR and CLEVRER. I set up the training and evaluation pipeline on Nautilus and trained FiLM for 80 epochs on 70,000 images.

sections.title: The results
paragraphs: On the full validation set of 149,991 questions, the provided FiLM checkpoint scored 96.8431%. My selected trained checkpoint scored 96.9552%. The pretrained NS-VQA model scored 99.8133%.
The full validation set includes questions used for checkpoint selection. These results are a comparison within this task, not evidence that I created a new state-of-the-art model.

projects.headline: Visual question answering.

projects.name: San Diego State
projects.role: Research with Professor Pablo Machuca and Jeremiah Symington
projects.intro: Studying what happens to lunar navigation estimates when measurements are farther apart.
projects.alt: Three circular lunar orbit test cases at 10,000, 20,000 and 30,000 kilometers from the Moon's center
projects.caption: The three higher-orbit cases from the saved simulation study. Distances are from the Moon's center.

sections.title: My work
paragraphs: I work on lunar optical navigation, measurement gaps, and crater-based estimates. The project builds on the team's source models and compares first- and second-order predictions as the time between observations grows.

sections.title: The study
paragraphs: The higher-orbit study tested 10,000, 20,000 and 30,000 km from the Moon's center. Second-order prediction had lower RMS angular error in all 33 tested orbit-and-gap combinations.
That result applies to these circular, two-body simulations. Camera pointing, lighting and the full navigation filter are outside this test.

projects.name: Voyager / Elodin
projects.intro: Measuring trajectory error and checking a heliocentric gravity correction against NASA SPICE.
projects.alt: Voyager 1 position error against SPICE over 144 hourly steps for two simulation chapters
projects.caption: Plotted from the saved hourly error CSVs for the two completed simulation runs.

sections.title: My contributions
paragraphs: I added position- and velocity-error telemetry to Elodin's Voyager example, then contributed an optional heliocentric relative gravity model. Those changes were merged in PRs #769 and #789.

sections.title: The comparison
paragraphs: Both saved runs completed 144 hourly steps. In this case, final position error against SPICE fell from 28.179 km in Chapter 1 to 0.840 km in Chapter 2.
The comparison uses the physical completed-step times; the database timestamps were one hour early. These are results for one simulation case, not a claim of navigation-grade accuracy.

projects.headline: Checking spacecraft dynamics against SPICE.

projects.name: Network recovery
projects.intro: Checking whether a network starts recovering after a delayed cell outage.
projects.alt: Saved outage-test comparison: current path moved 0 of 45 users, legacy path 29, reset control 28
projects.caption: Replotted from my September 29 research update. This is a simulator test; the reset control was diagnostic, not a confirmed fix.

sections.title: The test
paragraphs: I let a seven-base-station network settle, then forced BS0 down at tick 100. The simulator detected the failure at tick 111, but the current path moved none of the 45 affected users.

sections.title: What I checked
paragraphs: The legacy path moved 29 users. A control that reset the healing state moved 28. That suggests a state issue worth investigating; it does not establish the cause or a completed fix.
Alongside the tests, I review work on network self-healing, O-RAN control, and digital twins with Professor Tamer Omar.

projects.name: University of Tulsa
projects.role: Modeling work with Professor Joshua Schultz
projects.intro: Working through the geometry of a disc-and-thread soft robot.
projects.alt: Saved mild three-dimensional disc-and-thread geometry with a fitted three-section constant-curvature model
projects.caption: A geometry visualization from my saved Tulsa modeling update. Synthetic alpha/beta test; gamma, psi, and phi are fixed at zero. No experimental robot data is used.

sections.title: My work
paragraphs: I work on mathematical models and geometry visualization for soft robotics. This update places each disc frame at the shared thread anchor and fits three piecewise constant-curvature sections to the non-root frame origins.

sections.title: Scope
paragraphs: The saved run checks four synthetic geometries, including planar and three-dimensional cases. The drawing uses a 12 mm disc radius as a scale. It is an early geometry check, not experimental validation of a physical robot.

projects.extra_alt: Saved frame-origin and tip fitting errors for the four synthetic geometry checks

projects.name: NASA / python_cmr
projects.intro: Searching more than one satellite platform in a single query.
projects.alt: Actual platform method excerpt from the merged NASA python_cmr contribution
projects.caption: Code excerpt from my merged change in cmr/queries.py, PR #119.

sections.title: The change
paragraphs: I added multi-platform support to collection and granule queries. A single platform keeps its existing behavior; a sequence becomes repeated platform query parameters.

sections.title: Checks
paragraphs: The contribution includes collection and granule tests for multiple platforms and empty lists, plus the changelog entry. It was merged on August 23, 2026.

projects.name: OpenMDAO / Aviary
projects.intro: A smaller aircraft example that still runs a complete mission.
projects.alt: Aviary input-deck comparison: 476 advanced-deck rows versus 42 minimum-deck input rows, as reported in merged PR 1262
projects.caption: Replotted from the measurements reported in my merged Aviary PR #1262. The advanced deck includes 194 converted inputs and 282 unconverted legacy rows.

sections.title: The change
paragraphs: I reduced the advanced single-aisle example to a generic 42-input FLOPS aircraft deck, updated the beginner documentation, and added an end-to-end mission regression test.

sections.title: The result
paragraphs: The reported minimum-aircraft run converged with SLSQP in 12 iterations for a 1,906 nmi mission. The merged example is a starting point, not a calibration to a particular aircraft.

projects.name: OpenC3 / COSMOS
projects.intro: Letting injected telemetry keep its historical receive time.
projects.alt: Timestamp-handling code from the merged OpenC3 COSMOS historical telemetry contribution
projects.caption: Code excerpt from my merged received_time contribution, PR #3720. The formatting is condensed for readability.

sections.title: The change
paragraphs: I added optional historical receive timestamps to inject_tlm through the normal packet path. Existing calls keep the current UTC receive time; explicitly supplied timestamps are converted from nanoseconds since the Unix epoch.

sections.title: Checks
paragraphs: Regression coverage checks both routing paths, timestamp conversion, Unix epoch zero, and Script Runner forwarding. The contribution was merged on August 19, 2026.
